interactions.summary: Bromwich recites and interprets Macbeth's 'if it were done' speech, arguing that Macbeth already judges the murder as wrong, then traces how Lady Macbeth radicalizes the wish to step outside nature before the marriage turns into a compact of shared self-deception.

speaker_notes.note: The ASR garbles Lady Macbeth's speech ('stop up the access and passage to remorse') and briefly folds in a stray 'can't be undone,' but the interpretive point remains clear: Bromwich is citing her wish to become unnatural for the sake of power.

claims.claim: Bromwich argues that Macbeth's famous 'if it were done' speech is not a neutral hesitation but a fantasy of containing murder so completely that no consequence, earthly or eternal, would follow from the deed.

He says Macbeth explicitly enacts judgment on himself in the speech, since the language of 'cases,' 'bloody instructions,' and the poison chalice shows that Macbeth knows the murder is wrong even before he commits it.

Bromwich reads 'vaulting ambition' and the image of leaping the 'bank and shoal of time' as Macbeth's false belief that a deed can be made into a purely local event rather than something that stretches across a life.

He presents Lady Macbeth as someone who deliberately imagines herself outside nature, almost witch-like, in order to convert Macbeth's hesitant ambition into efficient action and the pursuit of power.

Bromwich argues that the Macbeth marriage evolves from Lady Macbeth goading him into murder to Macbeth later managing her, which reveals both their compatibility and their shared inability to separate agency from deed.

He generalizes Macbeth's self-deception into a broader account of ambition: ambition feels like an outside force that takes a person over and strips away the inward capacity to care about right and wrong.

signature_moments.moment: Macbeth is shown as judging and poisoning himself in the very language he uses to justify murder.
signature_moments.source_phrase: this even-handed justice commends the ingredients of our poison chalice to our own lips
signature_moments.why_it_matters: Bromwich's reading hinges on the fact that Macbeth is not ignorant of the evil he is choosing; he already tastes the returning consequence.

signature_moments.moment: Ambition is pictured as a leap that cannot land where it intends, because the very act of leaping becomes the fall.
signature_moments.source_phrase: vaulting ambition which o'erleaps itself and falls on the other
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This keeps the packet's central image of desire turning its own shortcut into ruin.

signature_moments.moment: Lady Macbeth's bid for power passes through a fantasy of stepping outside sex, nature, and ordinary human limits.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It sharpens Bromwich's claim that her role is not mere encouragement but an attempt to inhabit an anti-natural mode of willing.

signature_moments.moment: Macbeth's wish to know the deed without knowing himself exposes the impossible fantasy of uncoupling agency from action.
signature_moments.source_phrase: to know my deed, 'twere best not know myself
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is the packet's cleanest statement that deed and self cannot be separated after the fact.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Bromwich's key image for the way murderous instruction returns to the doer, making judgment an internal consequence before it becomes an external punishment.
The self-overleaping desire that tries to jump over consequence and instead turns its own propulsion into a fall.
Bromwich treats the phrase as Macbeth's fantasy that one violent act can simply finish itself on the spot without radiating consequence.

chronology_notes.note: The workshop remains in Bromwich's extended opening lecture on Macbeth; Jiang has not yet taken over the interpretive frame in this packet.

uncertainty_notes.note: The ASR is rough inside the long Macbeth quotation, so the packet tracks Bromwich's interpretive use of the passage rather than trusting every quoted word as clean transcript.
Bromwich's final generalization about ambition continues into the next context segment, so the packet keeps the claim modest and tied to the explicit lines already inside the focus refs.
